main_text.p: Bonum autem quod bona animalia appetūt finitum est: propterea illa quiescunt postquā ipsum consequuta sunt, Itaque omne animal motu cietur vel mente & opinione, vel appetitu, vt consequatur bonum, aut boni speciē.

Nullum tamen mouetur, nisi ante à sensibus alterentur membra eius. Ea enim iucundis obiectis calefacta ampliatur, sed triftibus refrigerata contrahi solent. Quemadmodum enim αὐτόματα rotulis quibusdam mouentur, quoniam semper aliud ab alio agitatur, sic animantis offa tanquam ligna sunt, & ferrum sponte se mouentium: nerui autem tanquam eorundem rotulæ: quibus ampliatis, remissioque & contractis mouetur animalis corpus.

Sed hoc inter se discrepant, quod sponte se mouentibus nulla alteratio euenit, sicut animalis partibus, quæ ob calorem dilatantur, & frigus comprimuntur. Dilatantur enim & comprimuntur, quod eis sensus qui alterationes sunt,Confestim inducantur. Quare quoties in corde quantulacunque fit mutatio, toties in animalis corpore & roboris, & palloris, horrorisque ac tremoris, harumque huiusmodi affectionum diffimilitudo adest.

Quod autem animantium appetitum mouet aut mentem, id est, quod in rebus agendis perfequendum est, aut fugiendū, nempe bonum & malum. Malum enim & quod dolorem affert, declinandum est: quod vero voluptatem expetendum. At quæ do-

page.notes: Transcription from a faded scan; the first paragraph and the sentence "Sed hoc inter se discrepant" were read with some doubt and may contain errors in individual letters (e.g. "ipsum"/"ipfum", "cietur", "Confestim" as printed "confestim"). The Greek words (αὐτόματα, printed "ꝯ" with a superscript, read here as "αὐτόματα") are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The printed text is reproduced with corrections of long s to plain s; the printed text contains "mutatio" and "inducantur" spelled as printed where visible. Some doubtful readings are not individually marked with [?] because the scan is too faint to decide; a fuller check is recommended.
